findings.location: SKILL.md Workflow and Rules; references/synchronizers-and-conditions.md, Keep the predicate test and wait registration under one lock
findings.problem: A while loop can test the predicate outside the associated lock, then register its wait after the signal. Volatile visibility and signalAll do not close that gap.
findings.correction: Trace actual waiter/signaler lock identity and predicate paths. Keep predicate testing and await registration within the same locked region, preserve interruption/timeout cleanup, and explain the early-signal schedule.
findings.evidence: Java 25 Condition/ReentrantLock API plus the executed controlled negative and positive cases below.

findings.problem: The prose named untimed tryLock as the only form needing conditional cleanup, although timed tryLock also returns false and can throw InterruptedException before acquiring.
findings.correction: Both boolean-returning acquisition forms establish a new hold only after returning true; false or interruption creates no new hold to release.

findings.location: SKILL.md lock selection; references/locks.md opening and pinning decision
findings.problem: The original unconditional pinning language was first narrowed to JDK 24+, but coordinator integration identified that this still omitted HotSpot's legacy-locking exception.
findings.correction: Qualify the JEP 491 behavior with default HotSpot locking. Explicitly state that -XX:LockingMode=1 permits monitor pinning in HotSpot 24–25, require deployed runtime/build/flag evidence, retain native/VM pinning caveats and the existing virtual-threads-internals referral.
findings.evidence: JEP 491 and version-pinned jdk-24-ga/jdk-25-ga globals.hpp plus continuationFreezeThaw.cpp. New claim is source-verified, not a runtime experiment.

evaluatorOnly.reproducibleControlledGrader: Main holds gate.lock with ready=false, starts the waiter and boundedly observes the waiter queued for that same lock. Main calls markReady reentrantly, then releases its original hold. A can enter condition wait after the signal; interrupt/join it under a bounded deadline. B acquires and observes ready=true without waiting. Record source/queue events; monitor methods are fixture observation, not production synchronization. The already executed isolated harness used explicit latch checkpoints and counted await-after-ready instead.
evaluatorOnly.limits: Finite schedules do not prove race freedom. Grader material remains separate from actor-visible task resources.
